name: Sustainability Studies, BA
degree: Bachelor of Arts in Sustainability Studies

requirements.label: A
requirements.title: Common Foundation Courses (15-17 credits)

rules.manualCheck: CHE 115 and ENV 115 are listed with the same title; treated as alternatives (cross-listed). The sample sequence shows them as one course, CHE/ENV 115.

requirements.sourceText: A. Common Foundation Courses (15-17 credits): AMS 102 - Elements of Statistics OR AMS 110 - Probability and Statistics in the Life Sciences OR BIO 211 - Statistics and Data Analysis: A Conceptual Approach; CHE 115 - Chemistry, Life, and Environment; ENV 115 - Chemistry, Life, and Environment; SUS 111 - Introduction to Sustainability OR ENS 101 - Prospects for Planet Earth; SUS 113 - Physical Geography Lecture OR GEO 102 - The Earth; SUS 201 - Systems and Models

requirements.title: Common Core Courses (12-13 credits)
requirements.sourceText: B. requirements.label: E
requirements.title: Communications and Writing Requirement

rule.manualCheck: Requires registration in the 0-credit SUS 459 and department approval of a term paper or laboratory report written for an advanced course in the major (including Readings and Research courses) from the preapproved list. SUS 459 is completed with a grade of S, which approves the WRTD requirement.

requirements.sourceText: E. Communications and Writing Requirement: The advanced writing component of the major in SUS requires registration in the 0-credit SUS 459 and approval of either a term paper or a laboratory report written for an advanced course in the appropriate major at Stony Brook (including Readings and Research courses). Completion of SUS 459 with a grade of S will result in approval of the WRTD requirement.

requirements.label: grades
requirements.title: Passing grades below C and Pass/NC

rule.text: No more than one course (4 credits maximum) with a passing grade lower than C can be credited towards the major. Courses taken with the Pass/NC option may not be applied to the major.
rule.reason: A one-course exception to the C-or-higher standard and the Pass/NC exclusion cannot be expressed as a minGrade policy without incorrectly failing the allowed exception.

requirements.sourceText: Note: No more than one course (4 credits maximum) with a passing grade lower than C can be credited towards the major. Courses taken with the Pass/NC option may not be applied to the major.

requirements.label: double-majors
requirements.title: Double majors within SoMAS

rule.text: Excluding ENV 301, SUS 301, SUS 305, and SUS 401, no more than 6 credits of 300-400 level course credits can be applied to two majors within the School of Marine and Atmospheric Sciences.
rule.reason: Program-wide cap on shared upper-division credits across two majors; no rule type covers it.

requirements.sourceText: Double Majors: Excluding ENV 301 - Sustainability of the Long Island Pine Barrens, SUS 301 - Technical Writing and Communication, SUS 305 - Collective Action and Advocacy, and SUS 401 - Integrative, Collaborative Systems Studies, no more than 6 credits of 300-400 level course credits can be applied to two majors within the School of Marine and Atmospheric Sciences.

fulfillment.sourceText: Completion of SUS 459 with a grade of S will result in approval of the WRTD requirement.

notes.text: Undergraduate Advisor: Nancy Black (nancy.black@stonybrook.edu). Program Director: Adam Charboneau. Program Office: E2361 Melville Library, (631) 632-9404.

ANT 120 is listed as formerly ANP 120; ANT 309, ANT 352, ANT 353, and ANT 408 are listed as formerly ANP 307, ANP 350, ANP 351, and ANP 401. Verify transcript codes against the current course numbers.
Courses marked * in the tracks have a prerequisite outside the major/track and/or require CHE 129, CHE 131, or CHE 152.
Other classes may be substituted with permission of the undergraduate director. This is not evaluated by the audit.

Study abroad experiences in Cuba, Madagascar, and the Turkana Basin (Kenya) are available. Students should talk with the major director about how study abroad coursework can fulfill major requirements.
Students completing the Stony Brook Curriculum must complete a WRTD course to graduate; SUS 459 is the department's WRTD route.
Sample sequence note: students in the Ecosystems and Human Impact track should take ECO 111; students in the Societies, Economics, and Governance track may take either ECO 110 or ECO 111.
